It adds and cuts money for substance abuse treatment, mental health services, and state psychiatric hospitals for fiscal years 2026 and 2027, and it adds 15 full-time jobs for Mental Health Services. Sections 7 and 8 took effect on April 2, 2026, and the rest took effect on July 1, 2026.

ID-2026-H928.aiSummary: This law adds a new section to Idaho law called the Merit-Based Health Care Act. It sets rules for Medicaid-funded health care providers on hiring, training, and public messages, and it bars certain diversity, equity, and inclusion practices in those settings. The attorney general may investigate complaints and seek civil penalties, and health care workers may sue for retaliation in limited cases. It took effect on July 1, 2026.

ID-2026-H810.aiSummary: The law changes the rules for people who want to run for state representative or senator in Idaho. They must live in the district for one year before filing and must have actually stayed there at least 120 nights during that year. People on active military duty get an exemption from the 120-night rule. It takes effect on January 1, 2027.

ID-2026-H542.aiSummary: Idaho’s law creates rules for large social media platforms that have at least $1 billion in ad revenue worldwide in one of the past three years. It says these platforms must estimate a user’s age after certain use levels, require a birth date when someone signs up, and get verifiable parental consent before making or keeping an account for a child under 16 or changing that child’s account settings. For child accounts, privacy settings must start at the most private level, and the law took effect on July 1, 2026.
